chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Identifying the tracks: Pinetop Smith, Leroy Carr, Speckled Red
summary: Hinton reads the track labels as music plays and Jones identifies the compositions and writers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: 1938. Let's just play a few tracks of that so people can hear it. I'm going to read the label here so the first one is. I'll tell you what. The first one is Boogie-Woogie. It's got a label that says author, Smith. Now who would be Smith? The second one is "How Long, How Long." How Long, How Long blues is by Leroy Carr, it says.
Leroy Carr, the greatest blues singer that ever lived.

The third track says "The Dirty Dozens" by this Speckled Red you were talking about. The fourth track is also by Leroy Carr, "When the Sun Goes Down." This is just Count Basie and the All-American rhythm section.
The first track was Boogie-Woogie. This is written by Smith. What Smith was that?
And the second track was How Long Blues was by Leroy Carr. Now what you want to say about that?
